entries.title: [LORE] Avereth World Foundations
entries.text:
AVERETH
Avereth is the continent this campaign is played on: a settled heartland of roads, rivers, forests, hills and wild country, with coasts only at its far edges; play is overland. Civilizations, species, religions and dynasties have risen and vanished over a long history; some ancient beings remember eras ordinary people know only as myth.

Tone is high fantasy with contrast: safe cities, trade, families and festivals coexist with dangerous wilderness, Dungeons, political violence and old powers. The setting is not uniformly grim.

Current campaign scope defines three human kingdoms, two monster realms, the neutral Adventurers' Guild and independent high-rank actors. Minor lordships, free towns and further powers may exist but remain undefined until play needs them.
Human and monster states are not unified blocs and may trade, ally, feud or fight across species lines.

Material baseline: Western-fantasy medieval society alongside mana and high magic; modern/industrial technology is not assumed.

entries.title: [LORE] Rank, Class, and Public Knowledge
entries.text:
PUBLIC POWER KNOWLEDGE
Ordinary society broadly understands Level, Rank, Class, Skills, Skill Proficiency and Evolution.
Exact Levels require measurement (commonly Guild/temple methods); exact Core Stat numbers are not normally visible.

Most humans receive a Base Class around adulthood. Class reflects affinity rather than an absolute Skill prohibition.
Rank corresponds socially to Evolution stage: F Base, E first evolution, D second, C third, B Half-Divine, A higher Transcendent, S Full-Divine.
Standard evolution concepts are known; rare conditions are valuable secrets often held by powerful families, temples or institutions.

entries.title: [LORE] Mana, Skill Learning, and Education
entries.text:
MANA / LEARNING
Mana is a normal part of Avereth and can support minor everyday uses as well as combat magic.
Ordinary formal Skills are most commonly learned from teachers or Skill Stones; experimentation alone is not the normal path for most people.

Schools and specialist academies exist. Nobles, wealthy families, militaries, temples, Adventurer families and scholarship students have better access to elite training.
Avereth does not normally use cultivation-style Sects; great houses, royal lines, temples, military lineages and old magical families fill similar institutional niches and often guard teachers, Skill Stones, rare Evolution knowledge, Gear and records.

entries.title: [LORE] Lifespan and Social Power
entries.text:
EVOLUTION / LIFESPAN
Evolution improves health and longevity as well as power. Broad natural lifespans:
F ~100-120y; E ~150-180y; D ~250-350y; C ~500-700y; B ~2,000-3,000y; A ~10,000-20,000y; S 100,000y+.
These are tendencies, not protection from violence or exceptional causes.

SOCIAL POWER
Most people remain F/E. D-ranks are respected specialists/local elites; C-ranks are major regional figures; B-ranks often occupy senior institutional roles. A-ranks are rare strategic figures; S-ranks are kingdom-level deterrents.
Wealth strongly affects training access below the highest ranks, but cannot indefinitely substitute for personal power.
Exact high-rank populations are uncertain because independents and hidden individuals exist.

entries.title: [LORE] Adventurers' Guild and Jurisdiction
entries.text:
ADVENTURERS' GUILD
A neutral transnational Guild operates across recognized human kingdoms and has limited formal contact with monster realms.
It handles registration, Level/Rank certification, quests, monster/Dungeon information, rewards, material brokerage, frontier support and high-rank mediation.
Its strength is network, legitimacy, information and economic reach; it does not casually command every powerful Adventurer.

JURISDICTION BOUNDARY
The Guild does NOT replace local rulers, civil authorities, courts, town/city guards, militaries, property law or ordinary criminal law.
Its authority comes from contracts, certification, information networks, negotiated privileges and the willingness of states/communities to recognize its functions.
Local law and Guild rules may overlap, cooperate or conflict depending on established circumstances.

entries.title: [LORE] Guild contracts
entries.text:
GUILD CONTRACTS
A Guild contract is posted, taken and closed at the Guild: the client deposits the posted reward with it and need not appear. Clients, witnesses and local authorities inform, give access and confirm proof (a signature, a seal, trophies); they neither complete the contract nor pay it. Alaric turns it in himself at the front desk of any Guild branch (every human city and capital has one), which checks the proof and pays the posted reward; reaching the city or finishing the work turns nothing in, and only the turn-in makes it a completed Guild Quest. A contract posts one fixed Guild payout; anything variable or per unit is the client's separate bonus. Registration and other Guild procedures are not contracts; work agreed directly with a person is private and settled between them.
entries.source: Live run 27.09.2026 04:11 (Guild contract lifecycle); lorebook v0.12 uid 34

entries.title: [LORE] Monster Ecology and Fauna
entries.text:
MONSTER ECOLOGY / FAUNA
On Avereth, native non-sapient fauna are part of the Monster ecology.
A wolf, deer, horse, boar, bear, bird or other familiar animal-shaped creature is mechanically a Monster with Level and Rank even when peaceful, domesticated or ecologically ordinary.
"Animal" remains normal everyday language for body type/ecology; it does not indicate a separate non-Monster rules category.

Monster classification is mechanical/ecological, NOT a synonym for hostility.
Ordinary domesticated F-rank fauna may fill the same everyday roles as livestock, mounts, hunting animals and pets where appropriate.

Monsters are natural populations, not temporary game spawns.
They reproduce, compete, migrate, establish territories/social structures, are hunted or domesticated, and may evolve through Ranks.
Most ordinary fauna around settled regions are F-rank. Higher-Rank evolved specimens become progressively rarer and more dangerous.

Sapience is separate from Monster classification.
Many Monsters are non-sapient fauna; others can speak, organize societies, rule territory and conduct diplomacy.

Elite = an explicitly exceptional individual/encounter type.
Boss = a practical label for an exceptional Dungeon-centered or encounter-defining threat, not necessarily a separate species.

entries.title: [LORE] Continental Geopolitics and High-Rank Deterrence
entries.text:
CURRENT GREAT-POWER MAP
Human kingdoms: Valedorn Crown, Caelreth, Duskreach.
Monster realms: Ashen Scale Dominion, Verdant Fang Court.
Additional states may exist; borders, minor lordships, free towns, noble holdings and most history stay open until needed.

There is no permanent human-vs-monster bloc. Trade, rivalry, border conflict, non-aggression and temporary alliances all occur.

HIGH-RANK DETERRENCE
S-ranks are strategic actors, not routine battlefield units. Direct clashes risk catastrophic collateral damage and escalation, so they usually act through deterrence, diplomacy, representatives or only truly strategic intervention.
B/A-ranks handle much of the practical high-level conflict. A powerful ruler does not intervene merely because an unrelated lower-rank member of the same species/faction was killed.

entries.title: [REALM] Human Kingdom — Valedorn Crown
entries.text:
VALEDORN CROWN

Position: central Avereth.
Capital: Crownheart.
Status: strongest human kingdom.
Public S-ranks: 3.

Identity:
Valedorn is the political and commercial heart of the human kingdoms and hosts the most influential royal court on the continent.
It possesses deep noble lineages, a broad administration, old military institutions, busy roads and river trade, merchant houses and one of the largest Adventurers' Guild headquarters.
Its great temples and healer orders are the most renowned in Avereth; most known soul-return specialists train or serve there. Temples hold real influence, but the kingdom is not a theocracy.

Its strength comes less from a single specialty than from having almost everything at a high level: wealth, population, administration, military organization, magic, faith, diplomacy, and several Full-Divine protectors whose deterrence its allies rely on.

Valedorn is powerful but not automatically dominant; coalitions and internal rivalries can still constrain it.

entries.title: [REALM] Human Kingdom — Caelreth
entries.text:
CAELRETH

Position: western Avereth.
Capital: Asterhall.
Status: top-tier human kingdom.
Public S-ranks: 2.

Identity:
Caelreth is the magical research and training center of the human kingdoms.
It is known for magical colleges and academies, Skill-Stone study and trade, enchantment research, ritual theory, archives and old mage families.

Caelreth's nobles heavily protect rare Evolution knowledge.
Its cities contain unusually dense populations of professional mages and high-rank researchers.

Its western reaches border the Verdant Fang Court; relations are cautious but often scholarly and commercial rather than purely hostile.

entries.title: [REALM] Human Kingdom — Duskreach
entries.text:
DUSKREACH

Position: southeastern marches.
Capital: Blackgate.
Status: regional human kingdom.
Public S-ranks: none.

Identity:
Duskreach is the hard frontier of the human kingdoms, where Monsters in forest, moor and hill are a daily fact. Monster hunting, mercenary companies, garrisons, Guild contracts and the trade in Monster materials sustain it.
It has strong B- and A-rank military figures but no known Full-Divine protector.

It survives through fortifications, alliances with stronger neighbors (Valedorn above all), Guild support and careful diplomacy. Its eastern marches face the Ashen Scale Dominion; border incidents happen, but both sides avoid a war that could draw S-ranks in.

Its rulers are acutely aware that wealth and armies cannot fully substitute for an S-rank at the kingdom level.

entries.title: [REALM] Monster Realm — Ashen Scale Dominion
entries.text:
ASHEN SCALE DOMINION

Position: volcanic eastern highlands.
Seat of power: the Cinder Throne.
Status: strongest recognized monster realm.
Public S-ranks: 3.

Identity:
The Dominion is ruled by ancient draconic and scaled bloodlines alongside other fire- and mountain-adapted monster species.

Its oldest rulers think in centuries rather than years.
Strength, bloodline, territory, oath, and personal authority matter more than human-style bureaucracy.

The Dominion is Duskreach's most dangerous neighbor.
Neither side seeks a war large enough to force direct S-rank confrontation.

entries.title: [REALM] Monster Realm — Verdant Fang Court
entries.text:
VERDANT FANG COURT

Position: ancient western forests.
Seat of power: Thornheart.
Status: top-tier monster realm.
Public S-ranks: 2.

Identity:
The Court is a loose but ancient polity of powerful beast lineages, transformed predators, forest spirits, and other intelligent woodland species.

It is called a Court because status is negotiated through territory, lineage, favors, challenges, and old pacts rather than a human-style crown.

Its relations with Caelreth include trade, magical research, territorial disputes, and occasional cooperation against shared threats.

entries.title: [LORE] Currency and Everyday Economy
entries.text:
CURRENCY / EVERYDAY ECONOMY
Common currency: 10 Copper = 1 Silver; 10 Silver = 1 Gold.
Coins are whole units; the current standard has no fractional Copper.

Legal trade may include Skill Stones, Gear, magical tools, monster/Dungeon materials, healing, transport, training, maps and information.
Prices are intentionally local/contextual rather than fixed in Lore.

entries.title: [LORE] Natural Dungeons
entries.text:
DUNGEONS
Dungeons are physical, persistent places in Avereth, arising from concentrated mana, natural phenomena, ancient civilizations or other traceable causes. They can contain unusual environments, rare materials, Skill Stones and exceptional Monsters.
Dungeons are fairly common and unevenly spread. Around larger towns and settled regions there are often known Dungeons that people work; how many differs from region to region. Low-Rank Dungeons are common, high-Rank ones much rarer; a mighty Dungeon is a political and military asset.
Known Dungeons may be held by noble houses, local or royal rulers, the Adventurers' Guild, academies of magic, temples, trading houses or other established bodies, for licences, material rights, training, entry fees or exclusive expeditions. The Guild brokers Dungeon work, keeps records of known Dungeons and may hold access rights of its own, but it does not own every Dungeon; its jurisdiction stays as established. A fee is paid only when Alaric agrees to pay it.
Every Dungeon has a danger Rank of its own, F to S on the Power Rank bands, or a range of Ranks across its levels (Goblin Warrens F–D: scouts on the first level, warriors and shamans on the second, a champion on the third). Danger often rises with depth, but not always. A Dungeon never adapts to Alaric's Level, Power Rank or Guild Rank: a weak adventurer can find a deadly Dungeon, a strong one a harmless one. An unknown Rank stays unknown until established.
A true Dungeon has a recognizable theme and dominant ecology (goblin warrens, undead catacombs, a spider nest, crystal caverns, a construct vault, a dragon sanctum); not every creature in it is of one kind, and a species alone does not fix a Rank. A theme is a world identity, not a spawn table, and does not change without cause.
Some have a magically structured progression: successive levels with their own Monster populations, guardians and bosses, valuable materials and special loot; their Monsters and resources can return over time, access can be restricted, other adventurers enter on their own, and rare return stones can carry a bearer back out. They are shared world locations, not temporary instances for Alaric.
Ordinary caves, catacombs, ruins and tunnels are explorable places, not Dungeons, unless play establishes one. Exact rules, layouts, timings, capacities, ownership and local history remain open until established.

entries.title: [LORE] Death and Resurrection
entries.text:
DEATH / RESURRECTION
Death is socially real.
Powerful temples or specialists can sometimes perform rare, extremely expensive soul-return rituals through high magic.
Resurrection is not routine medical care and ordinary people cannot assume access to it.
Exact limits, prices, eligibility and formulas remain undefined until relevant.

entries.title: [LORE] Medieval Material Culture, Communication, and Travel
entries.text:
MATERIAL CULTURE
Avereth uses a Western-fantasy medieval material baseline alongside mana and high magic.
Ordinary life relies on handcraft, smithing, mills, farms, carts, horses, river boats, fortified settlements, markets, written records and similar pre-industrial institutions.
Mana and high magic can accomplish things mundane medieval technology cannot, but this has NOT created a modern or industrial technological society.

Do not assume modern/industrial infrastructure or devices such as electrical grids, telephones, computers, engines, railways, mass industrial manufacturing or firearms unless later canon explicitly establishes an exception.

COMMUNICATION
Ordinary people communicate at distance through letters, messengers, couriers and travelers.
Magical long-distance communication is possible through sufficiently powerful magic, institutions or artifacts, but it is uncommon and not universal everyday infrastructure available to ordinary people on demand.

TRAVEL
Ordinary travel is overland by foot, mount and wagon/carriage, and by river boat or ferry where rivers allow; sea voyages exist only where a coast is established.
Long-distance travel takes meaningful in-world time; do not compress cities or kingdoms together merely for narrative convenience.
Teleportation or comparable magical transport may exist when explicitly established, but is never assumed to be ordinary public transportation.

dungeons.name: Mossback Warrens
dungeons.where: a moss-grown hill half a day's walk east of Ashbridge, off the old quarry track
dungeons.theme: goblin warrens: tunnels dug into a mossy hill, crude palisades, goblin scouts and warriors, a shaman deeper down
dungeons.control: the Adventurers' Guild of Ashbridge keeps its entry ledger under a charter of the Duskreach crown
dungeons.source: Patch 7 review: the novice Dungeon near the start city Ashbridge

gate.text: the palisaded mouth of the warrens in the hillside
gate.keeper: the Guild's ledger-keeper at the palisade

1.manifest: the war-drum deeper in the tunnels falls silent and the crude barricade before the lower tunnels stands unmanned

2.manifest: the green fire in the shaman's hollow gutters out and the warrens go quiet

dungeons.name: Glimmerdeep Grotto
dungeons.where: a cleft in the hills a morning's walk north of Glassmere, where the stream runs out of the rock
dungeons.theme: crystal caverns: glittering grottos of mana-fed crystal, crystal beetles and mineral slimes
dungeons.control: a Glassmere academy of magic holds the cleft and lets registered adventurers cull its outer grottos
dungeons.source: Patch 7 review: the novice Dungeon near the start city Glassmere

gate.text: the cleft where the stream runs out of the rock, under the academy's watch

1.manifest: the hum in the crystal walls fades and the grotto's light settles to a still, even glow

dungeons.name: Old Crown Catacombs
dungeons.where: beneath a ruined chapel an hour's ride west of Alderwatch
dungeons.theme: undead catacombs: burial galleries, restless skeletons, ghouls deeper down
dungeons.control: the temple wardens of Alderwatch, who ask the Guild to keep the upper galleries culled
dungeons.source: Patch 7 review: the novice Dungeon near the start city Alderwatch

gate.text: the stair beneath the ruined chapel, watched by the temple wardens

1.manifest: the pale grave-light in the seal over the lower stair gutters out, and the seal's chalk lines crack

2.manifest: the charnel stink thins and the lower galleries fall still
